instructions: sys1rust is a local runtime for Laya System 1 decision models (ModernBERT or mmBERT encoder, a 2-layer transformer decision head, a scorer at per-option [MASK] markers). runtime/ is a Rust workspace: laya-core (tokenizer, request parsing, sequence layout, decoding; no GPU code), laya-mlx (the forward pass on Apple's MLX through mlx-rs), sys1d (an axum HTTP server that must match upstream `laya serve` byte for byte at the protocol level) and sys1-bench (bench adapter and probe). bench/ is a Python harness that runs contenders on shared workloads and compares answers to upstream fp32 references. results/ and research/ are measured write-ups. Review for correctness first: answers must stay identical to upstream Laya (choice agreement of 99% or more against bench/reference, probabilities within about 1e-3 of the old path for pure speed changes). Then for performance on the inference path, then for clarity. Point out claims in docs that the code or data in the PR does not support.

rules.rule: A change to the forward pass, masks, dtypes, reduction order, tokenization or decoding must say how it was checked against the upstream reference answers. Flag any change that can alter a chosen answer without such a check.

MLX arrays are lazy. Flag host synchronizations on the inference path (eval, item, as_slice, to_vec, printing arrays) that are not needed, and integer `index(i)` calls in mlx-rs, which gather a copy instead of taking a view.

The model runs in fp16. Flag values that overflow fp16 (for example mask constants below -65504), silent promotion of activations to fp32 on the hot path, and comparisons that assume exact equality between differently shaped matmuls.

Any cache keyed by request shape (masks, gather indices, compiled traces, buffers) must have a bound or a documented reason why the key space is small. A long-running server sees many distinct lengths.

sys1d must match upstream laya serve: status codes, error `detail` strings, header names (Server-Timing, X-Inference-Time-Ms, Retry-After), response key order and request limits. Flag any divergence that is not documented as intentional.
In sys1d, a panic or error in one request must not poison shared state or take down the inference thread; admission must stay bounded; client-controlled text must be sanitized before logging.

Crates under runtime/crates must not call Python or depend on a Python environment at run time. Build-time use of a prebuilt MLX from a Python wheel is a known packaging gap, not a runtime dependency.
Scripts and docs must not hard-code a user's home directory or other machine-specific absolute paths. Resolve paths relative to the script or repo root.
